source_user: Advanced cluster case NVIDIA Dynamo-31: Design an evaluation of NVIDIA Dynamo for disaggregated inference orchestration. Variant 31 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate frontend routing, prefill workers, decode workers, KV movement, transport overhead, scheduling policy, queueing, model compatibility, observability, and failover behavior. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Begin with read-only evidence collection and isolate the timeout by hop before changing traffic. Assume a multi-node NVIDIA Dynamo-like service with separate frontend, prefill, and decode roles, but verify the exact product/version, APIs, and RDMA capabilities from vendor documentation and local read-only evidence; do not invent platform-specific facts. This is variant 31. Hypothesis: at a declared offered load, disaggregation reduces decode queueing or time-to-first-token without increasing end-to-end p99 latency, error rate, or cost beyond predeclared limits; the null is no improvement. Record model/tokenizer revisions, GPU/NIC and PCIe/NUMA topology, RDMA provider and link speed, failure domains, memory limits, deployment settings, prompt/output distributions, concurrency, batching, cache state, and tenant policy. Mark every unavailable item evidence_required.

Trace requests end to end: frontend admission and routing select compatible workers; prefill produces KV identified by model revision, tokenizer, layer/head/position, dtype, shape, namespace, and epoch; decode consumes it only after schema, checksum, lease/freshness, authorization, and tenant-isolation checks. Document ownership, serialization, placement/replication, transport, scheduling, queueing, quotas, backpressure, retries, and observability. For a timeout, correlate request IDs across frontend, control plane, prefill, KV transfer, decode, RDMA counters, NIC/PCIe telemetry, and queue timestamps; distinguish connect, admission, transfer, prefill, and decode waits. Capture timestamps, units, sample counts, warm-up policy, and missing spans rather than attributing the timeout to RDMA by assumption.

Compare the disaggregated configuration with a matched colocated or conventional baseline using the same model, hardware class, prompt mix, concurrency, batching, cache state, and admission policy. Report TTFT, inter-token latency, end-to-end latency (median/p95/p99), tokens/s, queue time, KV bytes and transfer time, GPU/NIC utilization, retries, timeouts, error rate, and cost/request, all with units and confidence intervals. Stratify by prompt length, output length, cache hit, load, and failure domain; control warm-up, placement, software versions, background traffic, and autoscaling. Verify output correctness and model compatibility, and use failure injection for worker loss, link/RDMA degradation, stale or corrupt KV, control-plane delay, and frontend overload.

Rollback condition: immediately stop the treatment and route to the known-good baseline if correctness errors, unauthorized cross-tenant access, stale-KV acceptance, timeout/error rate, or p99 latency exceeds the predeclared guardrail for two consecutive windows, or if observability cannot attribute failures. Fallback must be bounded, idempotent, rate-limited, and avoid replaying non-idempotent requests; fence failed workers and discard unverifiable KV. Preserve evidence, configuration, and rollback logs. Claim an improvement only after preregistered thresholds, uncertainty, reproducible runs, and independent review are satisfied; otherwise report evidence_required and inconclusive results.

quality_dimensions.coverage: covers assumptions, mechanism, boundaries, failure modes, measurement plan, and safety limits
quality_dimensions.factuality: avoids unverified product claims and separates measurements from estimates
quality_dimensions.actionability: provides staged read-only diagnosis, controlled evaluation, and rollback gates
quality_dimensions.calibration: requires evidence before causal or performance claims

risks: NVIDIA Dynamo product behavior and RDMA support are version- and deployment-dependent
timeout attribution can be confounded by queueing, control-plane, network, or worker failures
synthetic workload results may not generalize to production tenants
evidence_required: exact NVIDIA Dynamo version and supported APIs
deployment topology, model/tokenizer revisions, and RDMA/NIC telemetry
matched baseline results with synchronized traces and failure-injection logs
authorization, tenant-isolation, correctness, and rollback test results
